cards.text: Judah and his brothers have just sold their brother Joseph, and he's been taken to Egypt (Genesis 37:28, 36). Judah's the one who said to sell him instead of killing him (Genesis 37:26-27). About that time, Judah leaves his brothers and settles near a man named Hirah, an Adullamite.

cards.question: There Judah sees the daughter of a man named Shua and takes her as his wife. What people is Shua from?

cards.text: Then come the boys: Er, then Onan, then Shelah, born at Chezib. Three sons! I had six cookie cutter kids on one counter, and friend, I did not get ONE quiet night.
Judah gets a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name is Tamar. Remember that name, friend, and write it on your apron.

cards.question: But Er, Judah's firstborn, is ___ in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD puts him to death.
Tamar is a widow now. Judah tells his second son, Onan, to do his duty and raise up offspring with her. Who is that offspring for?

cards.text: But Onan knows the offspring won't belong to him. So whenever he sleeps with his brother's wife, he spills his seed on the ground so he won't produce offspring for his brother.

cards.question: The LORD sees what Onan did as wicked.

cards.text: So the LORD puts Onan to death as well. That leaves Judah one son: Shelah, the youngest.

cards.question: Judah's youngest, Shelah, isn't grown yet. What does Judah tell his daughter-in-law Tamar to do until then?

answers.text: Live as a widow in her father's house
Stay and serve in Judah's own house
Go home and marry someone else

cards.question: When Judah sends Tamar off to wait, he thinks Shelah is safe from what happened to his brothers.

cards.text: So Tamar goes to live in her father's house, and she waits. Friend, I know waiting: I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, till the dust had DUST.
A long time passes, and Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, dies. When he's done mourning, he and his friend Hirah head up to Timnah.

cards.question: Somebody tells Tamar her father-in-law is going up to Timnah. What is he going up there to do?
Shelah has grown up by now. Tamar still hasn't been given to him as a wife.
So Tamar takes off her widow's garments. What does she do to disguise herself?

answers.text: Covers her face with a veil

cards.text: Then she sits down at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah. Right on the road Judah's taking.

cards.question: Judah comes down the road and sees a woman with her face covered. What does he take her for?

cards.text: He doesn't realize she's his daughter-in-law. He goes over and asks to sleep with her, and she asks what he'll give her.

cards.question: Judah doesn't pay on the spot. What does he promise to send her?

answers.text: A young goat from his flock
A cloak from his own pack

cards.text: But Tamar wants more than a promise. She says only if he leaves her a pledge until he sends it.

cards.question: Judah asks what pledge she wants. What does Tamar ask for?

answers.text: His seal and cord and staff
His ring and robe and sandals
His cloak and belt and purse

cards.text: So Judah gives them to her and sleeps with her, and she becomes pregnant by him.

cards.question: Then Tamar gets up, leaves and takes off her veil. What does she put back on?

cards.text: Judah sends his friend Hirah with the young goat to collect his things from the woman.

cards.question: Hirah finds the woman right where Judah left her.
Hirah asks the men of that place where the shrine prostitute by the road at Enaim is. What do they tell him?

answers.text: No shrine prostitute has been here
She left for Timnah that morning

cards.text: So Hirah goes back and tells Judah everything. No woman, no seal, no cord and no staff.

cards.question: Judah tells Hirah to let the woman keep his things. Why?

answers.text: So they won't become a laughingstock
So she won't come asking for more
So his wife won't hear about it

cards.text: Judah adds, "After all, I did send her this young goat, but you could not find her." Friend, some folks would rather lose a whole jacket than make one awkward call asking for it back.
About three months later, someone brings Judah news. His daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and now she's pregnant.

cards.question: Judah hears the news about Tamar. What does he order?

answers.text: That she be burned to death

cards.text: As they're bringing her out, Tamar sends a message to her father-in-law. It says, "I am pregnant by the man to whom these items belong."

cards.question: In her message, Tamar says Judah's name outright.

cards.text: Instead she adds, "Please examine them. Whose seal and cord and staff are these?"

cards.question: Judah recognizes the items. Since he did not give her to his son Shelah, he says Tamar is more ___ than he is.
After this, Judah has relations with Tamar again.

cards.text: Then the time comes for Tamar to give birth. And friend, there's a surprise waiting.

cards.question: When the time comes, there are twins in Tamar's womb.

cards.text: As she's giving birth, one of the twins puts out his hand. The midwife takes a scarlet thread.

cards.question: What does the midwife do with the scarlet thread?

answers.text: Ties it around the baby's wrist

cards.text: "This one came out first," she announces.

cards.question: The twin with the scarlet thread ends up being born first.

cards.text: His hand pulls back, and his brother comes out instead. The midwife says, "You have broken out first!" Brand new to the world and already cutting in line.

cards.question: What is the twin who broke out first named?

cards.text: Then his brother comes out, scarlet thread still on his wrist, and he's named Zerah. Hold onto Perez and Zerah, friend, because the Gospel of Matthew names them both, born to Judah by Tamar, in its genealogy of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:1, 3).
